outcome: Obstetricians' opinions on elective induction of labor at 39 weeks gestation
Perceived feasibility, generalizability, and utility of elective induction of labor to prevent Cesarean section
cohort: Fellows and trainees of The Royal Australian and New Zealand College of Obstetricians and Gynaecologists (RANZCOG)
finding: There is heterogeneity among obstetricians' beliefs regarding the use of induction of labor at 39 weeks as a strategy to reduce the Cesarean section rate.
mod_finding: The study investigated obstetricians' opinions on using elective induction of labor (IOL) at 39 weeks gestation as a way to potentially reduce cesarean section rates.
